v1.feedback: The calyx-inversion concept clearly drove the design — petals flip downward, splay outward, and reveal a hidden crimson underside, which is a genuine formal swerve rather than a parameter tweak. However, the coup moment reads softer than 'théâtre' promises: the z-negation and 0.4 splay factor produce a gentle droop more than a dramatic flip, so consider doubling the invertedZ multiplier and adding a brief radial pulse at the coup peak to sell the moment of revelation. The crimson is tastefully gated behind the underside smoothstep, but its blend into the brown ink is so gradual it can be missed — a sharper uCoupHue sigmoid (currently linear with coup) would make the color swerve land as a true surprise rather than a slow blush.

v2.feedback: The coup lands — the calyx-to-inverted-petals flip with the snapping crimson reveal is a genuine theatrical moment, and the radial shockwave ring sells the kinetics. Two refinements: the flat-grid-to-cup morph at startup reads as generic parametric surface; consider starting already cupped so the dramatic beat is the inversion alone, not competing with a less interesting morph. Second, the crimson mask keys on vUnderside which is just smoothstep(nr)*petalShape — particles near the center stay monochrome even post-flip, making the interior look hollow rather than lushly revealed; blend crimson inward more aggressively or add a secondary vein-following crimson channel so the color swerve fills the form.
